thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in GPU driver resets across evg-gpu-pool-3 (driver_reset_count > 20/min). Rolling error codes include ECC/parity and 'Xid 117' logged on multiple hosts. Auto-page to #incidents (sev: high).

samir: seeing container OOMs and a couple runtime panics on node evg-03. dmesg shows repeated 'GPU instance reset' + Xid 117. stack traces point at nv-host reset.

maria: confirmed. Telemetry: 12 hosts showing resets in last 10m, 4 nodes flapping in and out of cluster. Latency spike for hosted inference; 503s on some routes.

leo: oncall? I can start triage if you're tied up. Quick ask: can we cordon the worst nodes and move inference traffic to reserved capacity?

oncall-sre: I'm on it — taking ownership. First step: cordon/evict affected nodes to avoid cascading failures. tagging as P0.

jess: initiating customer bridge for impacted paid customers (account-skinny and corp-ignite). Support, please prepare outbound communications.

support-lead: prepping message template. Will push initial note to customers in the bridge with ETA ~30m. No data exfil indicated yet (platform-only).

oncall-sre: mitigation plan: 1) cordon evg-03/evg-07/evg-12 2) drain pods gracefully 3) shift traffic to dedicated pool dp-1 4) collect nv-host logs and dmesg 5) escalate driver vendor if resets persist.

samir: running drains now. Command:```bash
kubectl cordon evg-03
kubectl drain evg-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

maria: also bumping autoscale on dp-1 to absorb extra requests. Patch config to increase capacity by +30% for next 60m.

leo: copying logs to /tmp/evg-03-reset.tar.gz and uploading to S3 for postmortem. Command:```bash
tar czf /tmp/evg-03-reset.tar.gz /var/log/nvidia /var/log/messages /var/log/syslog
aws s3 cp /tmp/evg-03-reset.tar.gz s3://redwood-incident-logs/1765432100/evg-03-reset.tar.gz
```

oncall-sre: I've restarted container runtime on evg-07 after eviction; node rejoined but reset counters still tick up. Attaching snippet from dmesg:```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 117, pid=0, GPU at 00000000:65:00:00
[ 1234.568120] NVRM: GPU reset done
```

jess: customer bridge up at https://meet.bridge.company/1765432100. Support message queued: "We are investigating GPU driver resets affecting inference latency. No data loss detected. We'll update within 30 minutes." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

support-lead: adding note for account execs for corp-ignite and a PSR check for payments workloads. They had 12 failed calls around 12:14 UTC.

nvidia-support: (auto) we've received logs and are parsing Xid reports. Preliminary suggestion: collect "nvidia-smi --query-gpu" snapshots and kernel oops traces for the affected timeframe. Looking for ECC parity patterns.

samir: doing live capture:```bash
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,gpu_name,utilization.gpu,driver_model --format=csv -l 1 > /tmp/gpu-snapshot.csv &
journalctl -k -b -1 | grep -i nvrm > /tmp/nvrm-log.txt
```

maria: telemetry team notes a correlated bump in background compaction jobs that increased memory pressure on those hosts ~10m before resets. Might be a compounding factor with ECC churn.

oncall-sre: good catch — throttling compaction temporarily across cluster. Command:```bash
curl -XPOST https://infra-api.local/compaction/control -d '{"mode":"throttle","rate":0.3}'
```

jess: ops note: we enabled automatic model-fallback for high-latency routes — routing to smaller quantized model variants to reduce token processing on GPUs. That reduced client error rate by ~40%.

support-lead: outbound update sent to impacted customers. Bridge attendees: billing flagged higher error counts for corp-ignite, engineering noted retry logic in client SDK increased apparent failures.

nvidia-support: we recommend collecting the output of `nvidia-bug-report.sh` from one of the affected nodes and a core file if available. Also ask if you can reproduce via stress test to trigger Xid 117.

leo: grabbing bug report now, uploading path s3://redwood-incident-logs/1765432100/evg-03-bugreport.tar.gz

samir: short-term status: 8 nodes cordoned/drained, traffic shifted, customer impact reduced to degraded latency. Vendor engaged. Working on rolling kernel/driver updates for nodes that continue to show resets.

oncall-sre: next actions — keep bridge open, continue log collection, coordinate with vendor for driver patch, prepare post-incident RCA once stable. Will escalate to infra on-call for out-of-band reboots if resets persist after drain/restart.

jess: thanks all. I'll keep customer bridge and status page updated. :thumbsup:

support-lead: closing loop to execs. Will attach timeline and affected accounts list to incident ticket.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity remains P1. Last auto-check shows reset rate down to 3/min after mitigations. Monitoring for 30m before de-escalation.
